scope: Local startup/security boundary gate catalog for NexusIM. These gates protect local development and CI-style checks; they are not a substitute for production identity, network policy, mTLS rollout, or external audit controls.

entries.name: DDD boundary imports
entries.note: Production api/app/domain/trigger/types packages must not import internal/infrastructure.

entries.name: cross-service private table access
entries.note: Production code must not read other services private tables except explicitly allowed shared contracts.

entries.name: future service boundary
entries.note: Only foundation-active services in service-registry.json may appear during the current AI foundation phase; later retrieval, RAG, agent, media, notification, audit, admin, and client-facing service directories must not appear before ADR/stage switch.

entries.name: Python AI worker boundary
entries.note: Python AI worker code must stay in the model / algorithm / eval candidate layer while Go owns control, state, persistence and audit.

entries.name: debug listener exposure
entries.note: Debug listeners must stay local/private and not become public ingress.

entries.name: public listener auth boundaries
entries.note: Mock auth and unsigned trusted metadata cannot be exposed on public listeners.

entries.name: grpc and websocket tls config
entries.note: TLS and client-certificate config must keep startup validation coverage.

entries.name: api-gateway startup gates
entries.note: Gateway-specific startup, auth, quota, and public boundary gates.

entries.name: api-gateway legacy descriptor migration gate
entries.note: Legacy descriptors cannot be removed until facade traffic, quiet-window, opt-in deadline, and exposure checks pass.

entries.name: api-gateway legacy observation window gate
entries.note: Legacy descriptor removal must use multiple clean observations with bounded gaps and no legacy or other exposure.

entries.name: api-gateway legacy removal plan validator
entries.note: Legacy descriptor removal plans must remain non-executing, low-sensitive, approval-gated, external-output guarded, and consistent with quiet-window evidence.

entries.name: api-gateway legacy removal plan gate
entries.note: Legacy descriptor removal plan writer and validator self-tests must remain covered by the api-gateway gate bundle.

entries.name: api-gateway quota snapshot gate
entries.note: Tenant quota snapshots must keep Redis mode, versioned/checksum policy, HTTPS, TLS/client-cert, freshness, and error guardrails.

entries.name: api-gateway legacy evidence manifest
entries.note: Legacy descriptor observation-window and removal-plan evidence must stay low-sensitive and reference external raw evidence paths.

entries.name: identity production key guard
entries.note: Production-like identity startup must reject legacy / HS256 gateway token mode and local shared identity key material.

entries.name: repair operator catalog
entries.note: Repair and cleanup operators must remain indexed and documented.

entries.name: repair operator safety helper
entries.note: Repair handoff writers must reuse shared low-sensitive actor, identifier, output-path, ad-hoc env, and hash guardrails.

entries.name: repair operator plan writer
entries.note: Operator planning must remain low-sensitive and dry-run oriented.

entries.name: repair operator catalog plannable coverage
entries.note: Every indexed repair mode must remain plannable through the low-sensitive dry-run planning path.

entries.name: repair approval request writer
entries.note: Repair approval requests must keep low-sensitive requester, approval id, reason, and external-output guardrails.

entries.name: repair approval decision writer
entries.note: Repair approval decisions must remain low-sensitive and tied to a valid approval request.

entries.name: repair operator approval chain
entries.note: Approved repair execution must require a valid request/decision chain.

entries.name: repair approval review page
entries.note: Static operator review pages must render only hashes and low-sensitive metadata, never raw env values, reasons, paths, payloads, or evidence bodies.

entries.name: provider replay handoff review page
entries.note: Provider replay handoff review pages must render only low-sensitive admin/workflow refs and hashes, never submit operations, call RedriveProviderFailure, mutate DLQ rows, or leak raw provider artifacts.

entries.name: approved repair invocation
entries.note: Approved repair invocation defaults to preflight and must not silently mutate data.

entries.name: repair batch manifest
entries.note: Repair batch manifests must only reference validated approved invocation summaries and must not leak raw reason or environment values.

entries.name: repair audit bundle
entries.note: Repair audit bundles must hash referenced evidence, remain low-sensitive, and avoid embedding raw repair evidence bodies.

entries.name: raw evidence output path guard
entries.note: Smoke/loadtest ResultRoot and OutputRoot writers must reject repository-local raw evidence output paths.

entries.name: external output root safety helper
entries.note: Shared output-root helper must reject empty and repository-local raw evidence roots while allowing external scratch paths.

entries.name: low-sensitive evidence metadata helper
entries.note: Evidence manifest append tools must reject obvious email, credential, bearer, JWT, and URL userinfo metadata, and roll back the original manifest if validation fails.

entries.name: message compliance proof manifest
entries.note: Message compliance proof manifests must contain only external proof references and hashes, not raw proof bodies.

entries.name: workflow compensation instruction manifest
entries.note: Workflow compensation rollback instruction manifests must stay low-sensitive, external to the repository, and free of raw payload or operator reason text.

entries.name: workflow compensation review page
entries.note: Workflow compensation review pages must render only low-sensitive bundle refs and hashes, never execute compensation or leak raw payload, reason, path, provider body, or EvidencePack content.

entries.name: capacity baseline evidence manifest
entries.note: Capacity baseline evidence manifests must reference H-drive raw summaries and repository runbook reports with low-sensitive metadata.

entries.name: capacity long-run campaign evidence manifest
entries.note: Long-run capacity campaign evidence must reference external plans and raw summaries while repository reports stay low-sensitive.

entries.name: resource snapshot evidence manifest
entries.note: Resource snapshot evidence manifests must keep raw snapshots outside the repository while indexing only low-sensitive summaries and reports.

entries.name: distributed smoke evidence manifest
entries.note: Distributed smoke evidence manifests must keep raw plans and summaries outside the repository and only retain low-sensitive references.

entries.name: observability evidence manifest
entries.note: Observability evidence manifests must keep local raw plans under the external result root while repository reports stay in runbook paths.
